Explanation: The parent needs improvement in all PEER areas. They prompt the child but often in very basic ways. Evaluations are minimal and often are just acknowledgments. Likewise, expansions lack depth and are infrequent. Repetition to reinforce learning is almost non-existent.

Use More Engaging Prompts:: Ask the child more open-ended questions that require critical thinking and imagination.
Example: "Why do you think Harry ran away from home?"
Evaluate the Child\u2019s Responses More: Provide clear and specific feedback on the child’s responses.
Example: When the child says, “It is Harry,” the parent could respond, “Yes, it is Harry! You recognized him even when he was all dirty. Good job!”
Expand on the Child\u2019s Responses:: Add more information or rephrase the child’s responses to build on their understanding.

Example: Child says, “Harry got dirty.” Parent could say, “Yes, Harry got very dirty from playing in the mud and running around. He turned from a white dog with black spots to a black dog with white spots.”
Repeat Prompts to Reinforce Learning:: Regularly revisit prompts and expansions to reinforce the learning.
Example: After discussing why Harry ran away, later the parent could ask, “Do you remember why Harry ran away from home?”
Incorporate CROWD Prompts:: Use a variety of prompts such as completion, recall, open-ended, Wh-, and distancing prompts to engage the child more deeply.
Recall: “Can you tell me what Harry did to show his family it was him?”
Open-ended: “What do you think would happen if Harry didn’t come back?”
Wh-: “Why did Harry bury the scrubbing brush?”
Distancing Prompt: "Have you ever felt like Harry when he was dirty and no one recognized him? What was that like?"
